text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed using specific blood tests that measure your blood glucose (sugar) levels. Doctors rely on guidelines from organizations like the American Diabetes Association to confirm a diagnosis.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests that measure your blood glucose (sugar) levels

list.snippet: A1C Test: Measures your average blood sugar level over the past two to three months. No fasting is required.
Diabetes threshold: 6.5% or higher on two separate tests.
Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) Test: Measures your blood sugar after you do not eat or drink anything except water for at least eight hours.
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): Measures your blood sugar two hours after you drink a sweet sugary liquid provided by the lab.
Random Plasma Glucose Test: Checks your blood sugar at any time of day. This is typically used if you are showing classic symptoms of high blood sugar.
Diabetes threshold: 200 mg/dL or higher combined with symptoms like increased thirst, frequent urination, or unexplained weight loss.

text_blocks.snippet: Except in cases of very high blood sugar with clear symptoms, doctors usually repeat the abnormal test on a different day to confirm the diagnosis. You can learn more about testing methods from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
